findings.text: Central requeue operation moves waiters from a source futex to a destination futex while optionally waking a prefix. It validates counts and PI mode, resolves both keys, optionally checks an expected source value, then under both bucket locks either wakes or migrates plain waiters or drives the PI proxy path before returning either a negative error or the number of affected waiters.

PI requeue wait path sleeps on a non PI source while prepared for migration to a PI destination. It validates distinct addresses and a non empty bitset, arms an optional absolute timer, records destination key and stack waiter, queues on source, then after wakeup distinguishes ignored early wakeup versus locked versus completed requeue and performs matching owner fixup and cleanup.
Robust list registration accepts only a length equal to the kernel known header size and on success stores the user supplied head pointer in the calling task futex area and reports success.

Proxy lock starter provides a schedulable wrapper that acquires the mutex wait lock with interrupts disabled, delegates to the internal starter with a wake queue, removes the waiter on negative outcome, then releases the lock with preemption controlled and flushes deferred wakeups before returning the inner status.

Reader semaphore operations expose a killable acquire that may sleep and reports interruption as a negative interrupted error, and a release that pairs lock dependency tracking with the internal read unlock.

PI requeue requires distinct source and destination identities checked first by address and later by key to cover shared mappings, requires exactly one requested wakeup, requires non negative wake and requeue counts, requires PI support at build time, and preallocates PI state cache before taking locks with out of memory reported as failure.

Queue elements carry a mode marker that must match the operation kind. PI requeue accepts only elements that carry a real time waiter and no PI state, plain requeue accepts only elements without either marker, and any element already bound to PI state is rejected. PI path additionally requires the stored requeue key to match the destination key.

When an expected value pointer is supplied the current source value is read while buckets are locked and mismatch yields a retryable contention error. Faults during locked reads drop bucket state, retry the user read without locks, and then repeat the whole key resolution for shared futexes or only the private bucket acquisition for private futexes.

Wait setup locks the hash bucket before touching the user page, validates the observed value against the expected value while still holding the lock, rejects same key source and destination pairs, sets interruptible freezable sleep only for the current task, and only then enqueues the waiter so that no wakeup occurring between value test and enqueue is lost.

Wait sleep arms the absolute timer when present, skips scheduling when the queue element has already been unlinked by a concurrent waker, skips scheduling when the timer has already expired, otherwise schedules, and always restores running state on return.

Robust list query defaults to the caller and when a process identifier is given resolves it under read copy update protection with missing tasks reported as no such process, pins the target, serializes against concurrent execution changes with a killable read lock, enforces read credential access control, then returns the native or compat head based on caller mode.

Reader ownership holds only when the semaphore count shows no writer component and the owner field carries the reader owned flag. The internal read unlock asserts expected magic and reader ownership in debug builds, clears reader ownership, subtracts one reader bias with release ordering, and warns if the resulting count is negative.

Requeue holds both hash buckets together with a reference that keeps the second bucket alive across the critical section, increments its waiter count before locking and decrements after unlocking, uses a paired double lock and double unlock primitive, and performs all chain walks and migrations while both locks are held.

Early PI wakeup handling requires the source bucket lock held and asserts that the waiter lock pointer equals that bucket lock. Only the source bucket is needed because the destination key cannot change while it is held and PI aware sources are unsupported.

Proxy lock startup serializes on the mutex wait lock with interrupt state saved, keeps preemption disabled across unlock and deferred wakeup flush, and reenables preemption only after wakeups are issued.

Robust list lookup holds the target signal execution update lock in read mode across credential validation and pointer fetch, uses a killable acquisition that can fail, and always releases the lock before dropping the task reference on both success and permission failure paths.

Read unlock disables preemption across flag clearing and count update, emits a contended release trace when waiters remain, and when the remaining state indicates only waiters without lock bits it clears non spinnable state and wakes waiters before reenabling preemption.

PI requeue proxy progress uses distinct outcomes for locked acquisition and idle with no waiter and in progress proxy with waiter queued on destination and done and ignored early wakeup and wait after interleaved wakeup. Locked means immediate wakeup and user space consistency, error means either nothing happened or ignore after interleaving, and zero means proxy state established pending completion at the caller after real time mutex queuing. Observed state names include Q_REQUEUE_PI_LOCKED and Q_REQUEUE_PI_IGNORE and Q_REQUEUE_PI_DONE and Q_REQUEUE_PI_IN_PROGRESS and Q_REQUEUE_PI_WAIT and Q_REQUEUE_PI_NONE.

Wait side dispatch after sleep has three handled outcomes plus an impossible case that triggers a fatal assertion. Ignore keeps the waiter on source and delegates to early wakeup cleanup, locked performs conditional owner fixup and drops the extra PI reference, done blocks on the real time proxy then cleans up the proxy waiter and fixes ownership with timed wait and interrupt mapped to contention retry where appropriate.

Observed queue element carries a key and an optional requeue destination key, a list node for bucket chaining, a task pointer, a bitset mask, an optional real time waiter pointer, an optional PI state pointer, a lock pointer, a private hash release handle, and a wake callback used with a wake queue.

Observed task state includes native and compat robust list heads under a futex substructure. Observed timer sleeper includes a task marker used to detect expiry and a timer object that is cancelled and destroyed on wait exit. Observed semaphore includes magic and count and owner and wait list state.

User faults on destination during PI proxy attempt unwind bucket state, fault in a writable mapping outside locks, and retry the whole operation when the fault resolves. Source value faults during compare follow a similar drop and reread and retry discipline to avoid holding spinlocks across pageable access.

Contended PI outcomes due to exiting owner or changed user value unwind buckets, wait for exiting owner completion where indicated, yield the processor, and retry to avoid live lock. Potential deadlock reported by real time proxy startup stops further queuing, releases the extra PI reference, clears the waiter binding, records completion status, and leaves residual handling to user space.

Early wakeup before requeue unlinks the waiter when still queued and decrements counts, then reports timeout when the timer marker shows expiry, restartable interrupt when a signal is pending, and a generic contention retry otherwise so spurious wakeups degrade gracefully.

Semaphore debug builds emit a one time warning with count and magic and owner and current task identity and contention state when invariants fail and then disable further lock debugging, while non debug builds define the check as empty with no runtime cost.

Public error outcomes observed include EINVAL for bad counts and mismatched modes and same address requeue, ENOSYS when PI is disabled at build time, ESRCH for unknown pid, EPERM for failed credential check, EFAULT for user access failure, and EINTR semantics for signals and killable waits. Additional retryable outcomes include EAGAIN and EWOULDBLOCK and EBUSY and ETIMEDOUT and ERESTARTNOINTR for contention and timeout and interrupt paths.

Wait setup uses TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE plus TASK_FREEZABLE sleep for the current task, wait completion restores TASK_RUNNING state, timer arming uses HRTIMER_MODE_ABS expiry mode, and robust permission validation uses PTRACE_MODE_READ_REALCREDS access mode.

Proxy trylock first reads the destination user value under protection and honors fault injection, returns idle when no top waiter exists, validates that the top waiter is a PI requeue waiter bound for the expected destination, prepares requeue state with contention retry on early wakeup, then delegates lock acquisition to the PI atomic helper and either wakes on immediate success or rewinds state on failure.

When additional waiters will be requeued the proxy path forces the user visible waiters indication during atomic acquisition so later unlock enters the kernel, while single waiter cases avoid forcing it to allow fast user space unlock.
